# THEORYs with `tags` `mathematical-statistics`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Mathematical statistics** — the theory of statistical inference read for itself — comparison and sufficiency of experiments (Blackwell, Le Cam deficiency), statistical decision theory, the sufficiency theorems (Fisher–Neyman, Basu, Bahadur) and bounds on estimation. Bayesian modelling is probabilistic-modeling (ADR-031).

| [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) v4 | More informative iff simulable by randomisation | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorem 8 with Theorems 1–3: for experiments with finitely many states and decision problems with bounded losses, α attains every loss vector β attains, in every problem, exactly when a Markov kernel turns α's observation into β's under every state. The direction from simulation to informativeness is Blackwell (1951); the finite converse is Sherman and Stein (1951); the general converse is proved in 1953. It is a qualitative order and says nothing about how much worse an incomparable experiment is. The record re-derived the converse for standard Borel outcome spaces (note of 2026-10-29); arbitrary spaces, which the paper claims through a quoted 1951 result, are QUESTION-321. | Active |
| [THEORY-157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md) | Sufficiency theorems hold in Markov categories | Fritz (2020), [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md), read in [NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md), Theorems 14.5, 15.8 and 16.3 with the definitions of Sections 13–15. Sufficiency, completeness and ancillarity are stated with copy, discard, composition and almost-sure equality alone. Basu's theorem follows with no further axiom; Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur use strict positivity, which Stoch has although it lacks regular conditionals. The match with the classical theorems is shown in FinStoch (Fisher–Neyman) and through bounded completeness in Stoch (Basu), not for measure-theoretic Fisher–Neyman. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-215](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-215.md) | Subcritical Hawkes processes are stationary | Brémaud and Massoulié (1996), [LIT-1035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1035.md), read in [NOTE-728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-728.md): Theorems 1, 2, 7 and 8, proved. Inhibition is allowed because the conditions use \|h\|. The conditions are sufficient, not necessary; the kernels are fixed in time; uniqueness is among solutions with finite mean intensity. In the linear excitatory case the condition is the branching ratio below one, but in the nonlinear signed case the spectral-radius quantity is a bound, not a branching ratio, and a bounded rate needs no bound on the kernels at all. | [THEORY-280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-280.md) v3 | Bisimulation metric estimable without a model | Calo, Jonsson, Neu, Schwartz & Segovia-Aguas (2025), [LIT-948](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-948.md), read in [NOTE-763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-763.md). Bicausal occupancy couplings are characterised by constraints that use only each chain's sampled occupancy measure over consecutive state pairs. A stochastic primal-dual method on them gets an ε-accurate estimate with probability 1−δ from O((\|X\|\|Y\|(\|X\|+\|Y\|) + (\|X\|+\|Y\|)log(1/δ))/((1−γ)²ε²)) independent samples per chain. The states must be observed and enumerable, the cost known, and the samples drawn with restarts. A single running stream and latent states are outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-308.md) v2 | Neural DV estimator is consistent | Belghazi et al. On a compact domain with Lebesgue densities, the supremum of the Donsker–Varadhan bound over some compact network family is within any η of the mutual information, and the empirical supremum converges to the population one almost surely. | [THEORY-534](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-534.md) | ML optimality was never one theorem | Stigler (2007), [LIT-044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-044.md), read in full in [NOTE-074](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-074.md). Fisher's 1922 proof rests on sufficiency, his 1925 proof on exact normality, and his private 1930 proof on multinomial data and smooth degree-0 estimators. Rigorous treatments (Wald 1943, Cramér 1946) came at the cost of unwieldy conditions. Neyman–Scott, where the MLE of σ² tends to σ²/2, is the failure Stigler weighs as practical; Hodges's superefficiency is possible only on a Lebesgue-null set (Le Cam 1953). It is a history: the theorem statements are reconstructions, and it says nothing about modern overparameterized models beyond one hedged warning. | Active |

The boundaries of a sequential likelihood-ratio test follow from the error rates by a two-line argument that needs only termination, so the test needs no sampling distribution. The approximate boundaries are conservative in sum. Either error alone may rise, but only by a factor 1/(1 − β) or 1/(1 − α) at most. Nothing here says how many observations the test takes or that it is optimal: that is [THEORY-951](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-951.md), and it needs i.i.d. observations. | Active |

The beam sampler is exact by construction ([THEORY-1037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1037.md)); how much faster it mixes is shown only in iterations and by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1046](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1046.md) | Data favour inactive sources at zero residual | Knowles and Ghahramani (2007), [LIT-1626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1626.md), read in [NOTE-1209](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1209.md). With y = g x + ε, x ~ N(0, 1), ε ~ N(0, σ_ε² I): ∫ p(y \| x) p(x) dx / p(y \| x = 0) = σ̂ exp{μ̂²/(2σ̂²)}, σ̂² = σ_ε²/(σ_ε² + g′g), μ̂ = g′ε/(σ_ε² + g′g). It is the Gaussian case only; the Laplacian case is the paper's (14), checked the same way. It concerns one data point and one source, with the loading known. | Active |
| [THEORY-1096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1096.md) | Garbling never improves attainable risk | Split from [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) by the status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)). [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md)'s equivalence needs a second proof of the general converse and stays Proposed. Ten of its twelve dependents used only its definitions (an experiment, a garbling, the informativeness order), or only the easy direction, that a garbling never helps a decision-maker free to choose any rule. The easy direction holds on any outcome spaces, and its proof is two lines, re-derived below under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2's ruling, which [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) keeps. It is Theorem 3 of Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md), and Blackwell's 1951 result. The finite converse is [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md), Active. | Active |
| [THEORY-1177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1177.md) | Informativeness equals simulability by garbling | The wide form [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) held before the twelfth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), Active, is its evidence. Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), claims the equivalence for any outcome space, through Theorem 2, quoted from his 1951 paper. The record's re-derivation reaches only outcome spaces that are standard Borel, since its last step needs a regular conditional distribution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1269.md) v2 | Iterated self-training tends to predicting zero | Wu, Yang and Sun (2026), [LIT-1884](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1884.md), Theorem 3.2, Corollaries 3.3–3.4 and B.1, and the projection identity of §3.2; read in [NOTE-1471](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1471.md) and checked by Monte Carlo in the spiked model. Active for the spiked closed form; the general concentration result (Theorem 4.2) is the paper's, proof not checked. It does not cover reused data, noise injected every round, or nonlinear students. | Active |
| [THEORY-1312](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1312.md) | Waveform shape can fake phase-amplitude coupling | Donoghue, Schaworonkow and Voytek (2021), [LIT-1999](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1999.md), §5 and Fig. 5D–E, read in [NOTE-1529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1529.md) from the PsyArXiv preprint, standing on Kramer et al. 2008 and Cole et al. 2017. Active: checked by a short simulation in which a sharp-peaked 10 Hz wave gave a modulation index of 0.021 between its phase and 25–60 Hz amplitude against 0.0001 for a cosine, and none in a single-harmonic or an 80–250 Hz band. It does not say any particular published PAC is an artefact, nor that broadband coupling far above the harmonics is. | Active |
| [THEORY-1337](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1337.md) | Band-power effects can be aperiodic 1/f artefacts | Donoghue, Schaworonkow and Voytek (2021), [LIT-1999](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1999.md), §§1 and 3, read in [NOTE-1529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1529.md). Active: the spectral argument is elementary (an aperiodic signal has power at all frequencies, and a change in its exponent moves every band), and the simulations and cited cases (the ADHD theta/beta ratio) are in the text. It does not say aperiodic activity is noise without physiological meaning; the paper calls it "a physiologically informative feature". | Active |
| [THEORY-1660](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1660.md) | Point estimates can't certify classifier fairness | Md Fahim Sikder, read in [NOTE-1779](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1779.md) (Read). FairCert is a black-box audit pipeline that turns per-group false-positive-rate (FPR) and true-positive-rate (TPR) gaps into finite-sample certificates. Five stages: a stratified split with a walled-off 15% audit set; LLM-guided discovery of candidate intersectional subgroups from aggregate training statistics (hypotheses), confirmed on the disjoint audit set; per-group error rates of the classifier's predictions; a certificate built from Clopper-Pearson exact intervals per group with a Bonferroni correction over K groups, which bounds the worst pairwise gap with probability at least 1−δ and passes if the bound is within tolerance ε; and, for failures, per-group threshold calibration with the TPR cost reported, plus a structured EU AI Act-oriented report. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1689](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1689.md) | Mutual information as one fairness template | Neighbour of [LIT-2451](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2451.md) — Monnier, George, Guyard, Tarnec & Kountouris, read in [NOTE-1739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1739.md) (Skimmed). A mutual-information-based template for fairness metrics and an in-processing mitigation (a regularizer inspired by the Prejudice Remover), covering independence- and separation-based notions, intersectional sensitive attributes and multiclass outputs, tested on tabular and image data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1719.md) | Aggregate fairness can hide subgroup bias | Boxer, McFowland and Neill, read in [NOTE-1741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1741.md) (Read). Models can satisfy a group fairness criterion in aggregate for a protected class while being biased against a subgroup of it (e.g. Black women). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2148](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2148.md) | Spikes above 1+√(N/M) pull out the top eigenvalue | Baik, Ben Arous and Péché (2005), [LIT-2986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2986.md), read in [NOTE-2241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2241.md): the BBP transition. The record's spiked-matrix claims use its threshold and outlier, but for real data, eigenvectors, more variables than samples and several outliers they rest on Baik and Silverstein, Paul, and Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi, which this paper corroborates ([ARG-145](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-145.md)). Proposed until a second reading confirms it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2149](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2149.md) | Spikes above 1+√c give own outlier eigenvalues | Baik and Silverstein (2006), [LIT-2988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2988.md), read in [NOTE-2245](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2245.md) (§1 only). The real, non-Gaussian, any-ratio, every-spike version of the BBP threshold and outlier, for limits. The record's spiked-matrix claims rest on it where BBP's complex Gaussian top-eigenvalue result does not reach ([ARG-151](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-151.md)). Proposed until the theorems are confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2152](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2152.md) | Low-rank signal outlies above a fourth-root bar | Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012), [LIT-2964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2964.md), read in [NOTE-2246](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2246.md) (§3.1 only). The additive, signal-plus-noise form of the spiked transition: the model the record's two-class mixture ([CASE-301](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-301.md)) and mean-shift step ([CLAIM-827](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-827.md)) actually use, with the same formulas as the spiked covariance model ([ARG-135](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-135.md)). Proposed until §3.1 and the theorems behind it are confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2153](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2153.md) | Spiked eigenvector overlap has a closed form | Paul (2007), [LIT-3006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3006.md), read in [NOTE-2238](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2238.md) (statements only). The eigenvector half of the spiked transition, for real Gaussian data with γ < 1, which [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) and [CASE-301](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-301.md) state and the BBP paper does not prove ([ARG-143](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-143.md)). Proposed until Theorem 4 is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2155.md) | Hyperribbon widths track Jacobian singular values | Transtrum, Machta and Sethna (2011), [LIT-3009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3009.md), read in [NOTE-2247](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2247.md). The geometry the record's [TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md) and [TERM-140](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-140.md) rest on. The widths are invariant where the Fisher spectrum is not, and match √λ only under conditions; the edges of the hyper-ribbon are where the metric is singular, which ties sloppiness to singularity at the boundary and leaves the interior regular. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2156.md) | Fits fail at the model manifold's boundaries | Transtrum, Machta and Sethna (2010), [LIT-2977](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2977.md), read in [NOTE-2240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2240.md). The letter that named the hyper-ribbon. Its explanation of the width hierarchy (interpolation) and its link to the spectrum (an observation in one model) are separate, and neither is a theorem; the fuller treatment is [LIT-3009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3009.md) ([THEORY-2155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2155.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2157.md) | LLC estimator is only calibrated in linear nets | Lau, Furman, Wang, Murfet and Wei, [LIT-2995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2995.md), read in [NOTE-2239](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2239.md). The estimator behind the record's learning-coefficient entries ([THEORY-1275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md), [THEORY-975](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-975.md)). The estimate is a free-energy slope at effective sample size n/log n, cut off also by the localizer's γ; the paper fixes β*, sets γ per experiment, and calibrates only in noiseless deep linear networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2170](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2170.md) | One update step leaves a spiked weight bulk | Dandi and colleagues, [LIT-2983](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2983.md), read in [NOTE-2258](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2258.md). The spike of one large gradient step is in the weights; in the features, learning shows chiefly as a reshaped bulk, with outliers from the means. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md)'s narrow point that the spiked picture of learned features is a theorem, and qualifies it ([ARG-166](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-166.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2171.md) | Teacher spike detaches by a BBP transition | Park and colleagues, [LIT-2990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2990.md), read in [NOTE-2260](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2260.md). A dynamical reading of the BBP transition: the outlier's appearance in the weight spectrum is a matter of step size and time, while the signal is in the weights from the first step. Its UTKFace experiments find the leading first-layer directions tracking the data's principal components only in the large-step regime. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) ([ARG-171](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-171.md)) and the rival reading [CLAIM-855](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-855.md) ([ARG-174](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-174.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2172.md) | Power-law degrees are rare in real networks | Broido & Clauset (2019), [LIT-2963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2963.md), read in [NOTE-2263](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2263.md). The record's network-scale evidence that a power-law shape is weak evidence of mechanism, and a ground of [CLAIM-803](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-803.md). Its test is of a pure power law above k_min; the verdict is disputed by Voitalov and others ([LIT-3041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3041.md), unread), who define a power law as a regularly varying tail, [TERM-142](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-142.md)'s sense 1. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2173](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2173.md) | Log-log lines don't establish power laws | Clauset, Shalizi & Newman (2009), [LIT-2987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2987.md), read in [NOTE-2262](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2262.md). The record's standard for fitting a tail, and the ground of [CLAIM-803](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-803.md)'s "fit first" clause. Its empirical lesson is that a power law and a lognormal are seldom distinguishable at realistic sample sizes (US city sizes among the undecided), and it defers the choice to mechanism without supplying dynamical tests. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2186.md) | Spike outliers can't increase with depth | Wang, Wu and Fan, [LIT-2984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2984.md), read in [NOTE-2274](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2274.md). At random weights an input spike survives each layer only past a BBP-type test, and depth can only lose outliers and alignment. After training the rank-one weight update exists for any step size, but the weights' top singular value separates only above one threshold and the kernel's outlier needs a second condition. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) as a third case of signal before outlier ([ARG-188](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-188.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2189](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2189.md) | CNN representations have low intrinsic dimension | Ansuini and colleagues, [LIT-2998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2998.md), read in [NOTE-2278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2278.md). Representations of trained CNNs lie near curved low-dimensional manifolds: a nonlinear estimate of their dimension is far below width and below a linear PCA count, which does not tell trained from random networks apart. [TERM-136](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-136.md) takes its intrinsic sense from this reading. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2243.md) | Threshold autoregression can detect hysteresis | de Jong et al. (2023), [LIT-3124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3124.md), read in [NOTE-2333](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2333.md). The test [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md)'s "individual data showing hysteresis" would need, with its conditions: a measured driver crossing an upper and then a lower threshold. Its depression case is simulated, and it reports no empirical psychopathology series. Proposed until its simulation results are reproduced or the paper is published as it stands. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2272.md) | Fairness meta-metrics can reverse rankings | Monnier et al., read in [NOTE-2364](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2364.md) (Read). A taxonomy of meta-metrics, m = f_a ∘ f_w ∘ f_c (comparison, weighting, aggregation), with synthetic and UCI Adult evidence that they reverse fairness rankings, and guidelines that match meta-metrics to the disparity pattern a context most needs to avoid. It takes the subgroups as fixed by prior deliberation, so it bears on how identified demands are weighed, not on who counts. | Proposed |
